stem.text: The function \( y = f(x) \) is a solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 3 y \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right) \), and \( y > 0 \) for all x. For \( x > 0 \), find the input at which f has a critical point and determine whether it is the location of a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither.

answer_key.label: The solution has a relative minimum at \( x = 3 \), because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( x = 3 \).

worked_solution.text: A critical point needs \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \). Because \( y > 0 \), the factor \( y \) is never 0, and for \( x > 0 \) the factor \( x + 3 \) is positive, so the only zero in the range is \( x = 3 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: zeros of the right side within the stated range

worked_solution.text: On the range, the sign of \( \frac{dy}{dx} \) is the sign of \( 3\left(x - 3\right) \) times a positive quantity, so it is negative just before \( x = 3 \) and positive just after.
Because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( x = 3 \), f has a relative minimum there.

options.label: The solution has a relative minimum at \( x = 3 \) and a relative maximum at \( x = -3 \), because the derivative changes sign at both inputs.
options.derivation: the zero at x = -3, outside the stated range, kept as a second critical point

options.label: The solution has a relative maximum at \( x = 3 \), because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( x = 3 \).
options.derivation: the sign change found correctly and then read the wrong way round

options.label: The solution has a relative minimum at \( x = 3 \), because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( x = 3 \).
The solution has no critical point for \( x > 0 \), because the factor \( y \) is never 0 when \( y > 0 \).
